title: How many tens and ones hide inside a number?
description: Tanvi packs pencils in packets of ten in Kolhapur. The video fills the blanks by taking the known part away from the whole number.
teaching_notes: One idea: take away the part you are given, and the rest fills the blank. Watch for a child who reads the tens digit as the whole count of tens.

source: Let Us Do (second set) 8 (a), (b), (c), tens and ones
video_script.why: The child knows tens and ones, but has not used take away to find a missing part of a number.
video_script.substitution: Take the given part from the whole number; the rest is the blank, regrouped as tens or ones.
video_script.anchor: Tanvi packing pencils into packets of ten at her uncle's stationery shop in Kolhapur
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu reads only the tens digit of sixty eight and writes six tens. Six tens and eighteen ones make seventy eight, not sixty eight.
video_script.payoff_line: take away what you are given

final_answer.spoken: five tens and two hundred and seven ones

video_script.design: Exercise. Hint: start from the whole number and take away the part given. The number 983, done in the book, sits on the board as packets and loose pencils.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; packets of ten pencils and some loose pencils on a shop counter; two statements with an empty blank each: 68 = __ Tens + 18 Ones and 607 = 4 Hundreds + __ Ones

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.story: packets of ten pencils appear on a shop counter
marks.ask: two statements with an empty blank in each appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Tanvi packs pencils into packets of ten at her uncle's shop in Kolhapur.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Some blanks must be filled to say how many tens and ones a number has.

beats.on_screen: the items hold still and the anchor gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the done example: 983 shown as 90 packets of ten (900 pencils) and 83 loose pencils; a note says start from the whole number and take away the part you are given

marks.packs: 90 packets glow as 900, 83 loose pencils sit beside them

narration: <bookmark mark='done'/>Your book shows nine hundred and eighty three as ninety tens and eighty three ones.
<bookmark mark='packs'/>Ninety packets of ten hold nine hundred pencils, and eighty three pencils are loose.
<bookmark mark='hint'/>Start from the whole number, and take away the part you are given. Try again with this.

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows 68 = 6 Tens + 18 Ones; a sum 60 + 18 = 78 appears beside 68 and the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.chintu: Chintu's bubble appears with the wrong blank
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The six in sixty eight is the tens digit, so the blank is six tens.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Six tens is sixty, and sixty plus eighteen is seventy eight.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That is more than sixty eight, so six tens cannot be right.

beats.on_screen: the rule line appears; the board shows 68 − 18 = 50 and then 50 = 5 Tens

marks.tens: 50 regroups into 5 Tens and the blank shows 5 Tens

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Take away what you are given, and what is left fills the blank.
<bookmark mark='sub'/>Sixty eight take away eighteen leaves fifty.
<bookmark mark='tens'/>Fifty is five tens, because each ten holds ten ones.

beats.on_screen: the board shows 4 Hundreds = 400, then 607 − 400 = 207, and the blank shows 207 Ones
narration: <bookmark mark='sub'/>Six hundred and seven take away four hundred leaves two hundred and seven.
<bookmark mark='ones'/>The blank is two hundred and seven ones, because the hundreds are already counted.

beats.on_screen: two checks side by side: 50 + 18 = 68 and 400 + 207 = 607

marks.check: the words add the two parts appear

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, add the two parts and see if they make the whole number.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Fifty plus eighteen makes sixty eight.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Four hundred plus two hundred and seven makes six hundred and seven.
